purpose: Preserve the unpadded valid Header A length for short extended OMCI while retaining the padded DMA buffer span.
root_cause: OMCI producer pads short wire messages to48 bytes before NI submission. Native DMA unconditionally used this padded skb length plus16-byte internal container as Header A pkt_size. Original DAL supplies wire length plus16 in Header A, even when skb is padded to64 bytes; actual __rtk_ni_start_xmit copies the supplied Header A unchanged.
fix: OMCI sets the actual Header A pkt_size independently of its padded skb length.
DMA honors a supplied Header A pkt_size; callers without one retain automatic length calculation.
DMA-LSO packet size, descriptor buffer length and zero padding retain the padded span; frame structure layout and public symbol signatures are unchanged.

verification.cases: Two XG modes, baseline plus extended content0/32/34/76 bytes. Four before-fix header mismatches; all10 after-fix headers match. Internal prefix, body, modeled MIC and DMA spans match in every case.
verification.other_NI_traffic: Three direct production-DMA default-length checks: Ethernet minimum padding, Ethernet plus container and raw plus container.
verification.scope: Actual original DAL OMCI TX and native OMCI producer plus DMA TX function. Allocator, MIC bytes, NI completion and submission, locks, MMIO and skb primitives are modeled. REA __rtk_ni_start_xmit separately shows the supplied Header A is copied unchanged. No optical transmission or cryptographic correctness claim.

additional_research.Alloc_ID: REA original default Assign-Alloc-ID parser records scope; its extra software T-CONT adjustment is controlled by an activation-debug bit. No evidence supports adding that debug override to native normal activation.
additional_research.ONU_ID: REA original Assign-ONU-ID reads the hardware-owned T-CONT0 and programs XGEM1..7; it does not manually overwrite T-CONT0 in this handler. No speculative T-CONT0 setter added.
additional_research.MIC: Original OMCI MIC input is direction byte followed by OMCI body, consistent with native direction/body framing.

limits: MIC bytes and NI submission/completion are modeled in the transport replay; this turn does not validate cryptographic correctness or physical transmission.
No XGPON OLT traffic or proof that this defect caused the peer approximately50-second reset or reported -110.
Two changed ARM64 objects compiled, no full kernel link, firmware build, full tests, deployment, commit or push.
Goal remains active: whole-path XGPON correctness and physical registration/business behavior are not established by this scoped correction.
